newsitem.title: JAPAN: Ichiyoshi Sec accepts Norway bond cancellations.
newsitem.headline: Ichiyoshi Sec accepts Norway bond cancellations.

text.p: Ichiyoshi Securities will accept the cancellation of contracts by individual investors who committed to buy 5.1 percent dual-currency bonds issued by Norway's Eksportfinans, a Ichiyoshi official said on Friday.
Ichiyoshi said it would permit investors to cancel their contracts as the bond, which contains special foreign exchange options, broke below its face value after the dollar fell below 115.80 yen.
"We decided to accept the cancellations by investors after the dollar dropped below the knock out level of 115.80 yen during the subscription period," the official said.
The dollar fell as low as 114.70 yen in Europe on Thursday. It stood at 115.43/53 yen at 1022 GMT on Friday.
The brokerage aimed to sell five billion yen worth of the bonds. The subscription period started on May 12 and was scheduled to end May 28. The payment date was scheduled for May 29.
The coupon of the bond was to be paid in yen, while redemption was to be in U.S. dollars, under special terms.
The terms were that holders of the bonds were to receive $3,962.05 for each 500,000-yen bond held to maturity if the bond fell below 115.80 yen.

But if the dollar stayed above that level by the maturity date in the six-month period then holders would have receive the face value of each 500,000 yen bond at maturity and collect the coupon of 5.1 percent.
